pages.text: $(bold)The merchant$() trades both ways: he buys what his town needs for emeralds, and his Buy tab sells what it has to spare. A town only sells above what it wants to keep, so a rich neighbour's shelf tells you what it is sitting on.$(br2)Buying back always costs more than you sold for. What a merchant wants to buy shows what the town is planning.

$(bold)The Noble$() keeps a contract board (sneak-click him): cull monsters, stand a night watch, haul a material. Finished work pays emeralds and $(bold)standing$() with that faction, and only that one.$(br2)Standing opens a faction's better contracts, its shop and eventually its gates.

$(bold)Losing standing:$() killing a faction's people costs it. Far enough down and it posts a $(bold)bounty$() on you that other players can take, and its soldiers attack on sight. A player-run faction's leader can pardon you; a town run by the villagers never forgets.$(br2)Check where you stand with /vrcontracts standing.
